title: Comprehensive histone epigenetics: A mass spectrometry based screening assay to measure epigenetic toxicity
author: Verhelst, De Clerck, et al.
materials: After harvesting the cell cultures, histones were extracted as described by Govaert et al. [15] (cf. Protocol 1 in supplementary material). First, the nuclei were isolated from frozen cell pellets by resuspension in hypotonic lysis buffer (HLB). A number of 106 cells was resuspended in 200 µL of HLB (10 mM Tris–HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM KCl, 1.5 mM MgCl2) supplemented with 1 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), Halt protease, 1 V/V% EDTA-free phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (788,441, Thermo Fisher), and 1 V/V% phosphatase inhibitor cocktails II and III (P5726 and P0044, Sigma-Aldrich). Subsequently, this mixture was incubated for 30 min on a rotator at 4°C after which the nuclei were pelleted, and the supernatant was discarded. The pellet was resuspended in 125 µL of 0.4 N HCl and incubated for 30 min on a rotator at 4°C. Next, the histones were precipitated with 33% trichloroacetic acid on ice for 30 min. A histone-load corresponding to 400,000 cells was quantified by gel-electrophoresis on an 8–16% TGX gel (Biorad) (cf. Protocol 2 in supplementary material).

steps.title: Isolate nuclei from frozen cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend 1 × 10⁶ frozen cells in 200 µL hypotonic lysis buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM KCl, 1.5 mM MgCl₂) containing 1 mM DTT, Halt protease inhibitor, 1 % v/v EDTA‑free phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Thermo Fisher 788,441) and 1 % v/v phosphatase inhibitor cocktails II and III (Sigma‑Aldrich P5726, P0044); incubate 30 min on a rotator at 4 °C; pellet nuclei by centrifugation and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Extract and precipitate histones
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclear pellet in 125 µL 0.4 N HCl and incubate 30 min on a rotator at 4 °C; precipitate histones by adding 33 % trichloroacetic acid on ice for 30 min; quantify a histone load corresponding to 400 000 cells by 8–16 % TGX gel electrophoresis.

steps.title: Vacuum‑dry histones and dissolve in TEAB
steps.instruction: Vacuum‑dry the purified histones; dissolve the dried material in 20 µL 1 M triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB) buffer, pH 8.5.

steps.title: First propionylation of histones
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL propionylation reagent (propionic anhydride : 2‑propanol 1 : 80 v/v) to the TEAB solution; incubate 30 min at room temperature (RT).

steps.title: Second propionylation (water incubation)
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Milli‑Q water; incubate 30 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Overnight trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the sample overnight at 37 °C with trypsin at an enzyme‑to‑histone mass ratio of 1 : 20 (m/m) in 500 mM TEAB containing 1.0 mM CaCl₂ and 5 % acetonitrile (ACN).

steps.title: Cap peptide N‑termini with repeat propionylation
steps.instruction: Repeat the propionylation reaction (steps 4 and 5) to cap newly formed peptide N‑termini.

steps.title: Reverse overpropionylation with hydroxylamine
steps.instruction: Resuspend the vacuum‑dried sample in 50 µL 0.5 M hydroxylamine (NH₂OH) and 15 µL NH₄OH, adjust to pH 12, and incubate 20 min at RT.

steps.title: Acidify and vacuum‑dry propionylated peptides
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL 100 % formic acid (FA) to the reaction; vacuum‑dry the resulting propionylated histone peptides for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Import raw LC‑MS/MS files into Progenesis
steps.instruction: Import all .wiff files from the data‑dependent acquisition (DDA) runs into Progenesis QIP 3.0.2.

steps.title: Align runs, peak pick, and filter ions
steps.instruction: Automatically align the imported runs, perform peak picking, and filter out ions with a charge state of +1.

steps.title: Verify sample normalization
steps.instruction: Check the normalization output to ensure adequate loading of each sample.

steps.title: Generate custom FASTA database from top spectra
steps.instruction: For each feature, select the twenty MS/MS spectra closest to the elution apex, merge them into a single *.mgf file, and run a standard Mascot search (no variable modifications) against the Human SwissProt database supplemented with the cRAP contaminants; use the identified proteins to build a custom FASTA database.

steps.title: Verify beta‑galactosidase and propionylation efficiency
steps.instruction: Perform a Mascot search using trypsin as the enzyme and no fixed modifications to confirm the presence of β‑galactosidase and assess the efficiency of the propionylation reaction.

steps.title: Mascot search for nine histone PTMs
steps.instruction: Export, for each feature, the three MS/MS spectra closest to the elution apex into a *.mgf file and search with Mascot using: precursor tolerance 10 ppm, fragment tolerance 50 ppm; enzyme specificity Arg‑C with up to one missed cleavage; variable modifications – acetylation, butyrylation, crotonylation, trimethylation, formylation on K; methylation on R; dimethylation on K and R; deamidation on N, Q and R; oxidation of M; fixed modifications – N‑terminal propionylation and propionylation on K.

steps.title: Import identifications, validate histone features, re‑search
steps.instruction: Import the Mascot identifications into Progenesis QIP 3.0, manually validate histone peptide features, export a new *.mgf file (rank 3) and repeat the Mascot search with the same parameters; this yields the final set of identified histone proteins (H3, H4, H1, H2A).

steps.title: Import final results and calculate relative abundance
steps.instruction: Import the final *.xml file into Progenesis QIP 3.0, obtain spectrum matches (e.g., 2277 total, 240 histone peptide ions), and calculate relative abundance (RA) for each peptidoform by dividing its area‑under‑the‑curve (AUC) by the sum of AUCs of all observed forms of the same peptide.
